gp-start.speaker: S01
gp-start.narration: Graham Pike keeps straightening a pen that is already straight.
gp-start.text: Twenty-two years, Detective, and never so much as a pound out of place. Now this. Whatever you need.

variants.text: Have you read the report? Forty boxes, Detective. I'd rather not explain it from the beginning to someone who hasn't.

choices.label: Ask how he found the vault
Ask who can open the vault
Ask about the locksmith across the road

gp-found.speaker: S01
gp-found.text: Five past nine. The door, the time lock, the alarm: everything exactly as I left it on Thursday. And behind the door, forty drawers hanging open like mouths.

gp-weekend.speaker: S01
gp-weekend.text: At home. With my wife. The whole holiday. I didn't come near the place.

gp-combo.speaker: S01
gp-combo.text: Nobody alone. I hold one half, the chief clerk the other, in sealed envelopes. The only person who ever sees both is the auditor, and only for a few minutes, once a quarter. Mr Thorne did it on Thursday.

gp-kemp.speaker: S01
gp-kemp.text: Walter Kemp did twelve years for safes and then opened a shop fifty yards from my vault. I've said so to your constable. I've said so to head office, twice.

gp-e005.speaker: S01
gp-e005.text: My spectacles. I left my reading glasses in the office on Thursday and I couldn't do the crossword. The guard walked me in and out. Six minutes. I didn't go downstairs. I didn't say because it looks exactly like this.

gp-e016.speaker: S01
gp-e016.text: Mr Thorne was very thorough on Thursday. He opened both envelopes and resealed them. That's the procedure. He's been doing it for twenty years.

gp-unmoved.speaker: S01
gp-unmoved.text: I'm sorry, I don't follow. What has that to do with the branch?

rd-start.speaker: S02
rd-start.narration: Rosa Delgado doesn't put down her screwdriver.
rd-start.text: I know how it looks. Alarm engineer, Saturday, vault gets done Saturday night. Ask your questions and let me get back to work.

choices.label: Ask who booked the service call
Ask who can bypass the vault sensor

rd-sat.speaker: S02
rd-sat.text: Four o'clock, doors and windows, out by quarter to five. Then my cousin's wedding. I danced till one. Fifty people watched me do the conga.

rd-booked.speaker: S02
rd-booked.text: Head office booked it on Thursday. Someone from audit, very particular: full sensor test, vault included, and it had to be the weekend. I thought it was odd. Head office never wants weekends; they don't like paying the overtime.

rd-codes.speaker: S02
rd-codes.text: Three codes will bypass that vault sensor: the manager's, mine, and head office's audit code. Four-seven. Mine was used at four in the afternoon, with the front keypad. The log will tell you who used what at the back.

rd-e003.speaker: S02
rd-e003.text: Of course I was at the vault sensor at twenty past four. It was on the ticket. I lied because I knew what it would look like. And look who entered code four-seven at eight minutes past eleven. That's not my code.

rd-e010.speaker: S02
rd-e010.text: Maria's wedding. Ring her mother. She'll tell you more than you want to know.

rd-unmoved.speaker: S02
rd-unmoved.text: That's not an alarm. I do alarms.

wk-start.speaker: S03
wk-start.narration: Walter Kemp finishes cutting the key before he looks at you.
wk-start.text: Go on, then. Convicted safe-breaker, fifty yards from a vault. I'd arrest me too, if I were lazy.

choices.label: Ask where he was on Saturday night
Ask what he saw on Harbour Street that night
Ask how he'd open that vault

wk-record.speaker: S03
wk-record.text: Twelve years. I came out and opened a key shop across the road from a bank. That's either very stupid or very honest, and I was never stupid.

wk-sat.speaker: S03
wk-sat.text: In bed by ten. My van was nowhere near that bank.

wk-saw.speaker: S03
wk-saw.text: Saturday, gone eleven, I got up for a glass of water. A big Rover crawled down the side of the bank to the loading bay with its lights off. Nobody drives like that unless they don't want to be seen. Grey, or silver. A head-office sort of car.

wk-vault.speaker: S03
wk-vault.text: You don't pick that vault. Nobody picks that vault. You get the combination, you wait out the time lock or you know the service override, and you silence the sensor with a code. That's not a thief. That's someone with a desk at head office.

wk-e008.speaker: S03
wk-e008.text: I live over the shop! My van lives on this street! I got a ticket for parking outside my own front door. Look at the rent book.

wk-unmoved.speaker: S03
wk-unmoved.text: Never seen it. And I'd tell you if I had. I'm out of the business of lying.

et-start.speaker: S04
et-start.narration: Edwin Thorne pours the tea himself and slides a cup across to you.
et-start.text: Edwin Thorne, Head Office Audit. A dreadful business. I audited that branch only last Thursday, so I'll help however I can.

variants.text: My sister is seventy-one, Detective. I've told her not to speak to you. Ask me whatever you like, but leave her out of it.

choices.label: Ask where he spent the weekend
Threaten to charge his sister as an accomplice

et-weekend.speaker: S04
et-weekend.text: At my sister Margaret's in Millbrook, from Thursday evening until this morning. I didn't stir. You're very welcome to telephone her; she'll be delighted to have someone to talk to.

et-audit.speaker: S04
et-audit.text: Routine. Cash, ledgers, and the combination envelopes: opened, verified, resealed, signed. Seven minutes. I've done it a hundred times.

et-pike.speaker: S04
et-pike.narration: He lowers his voice as if the walls were listening.
et-pike.text: I'd rather not say it. But Mr Pike's personal account is badly overdrawn, and his books were untidy on Thursday. If I were you, I'd look at who needs the money.

et-kemp.speaker: S04
et-kemp.text: A convicted safe-breaker opposite a vault. I wrote a memorandum about it in 1982. Nobody listened.

et-threat.speaker: S04
et-threat.narration: His cup goes down on the saucer with a crack.
et-threat.text: My sister is seventy-one years old. You will not frighten her. I'll make sure she speaks to nobody without a solicitor present.

et-e012.speaker: S04
et-e012.text: Margaret is seventy-one and she naps in the afternoons. Perhaps I went for a drive. People drive. It's a holiday.

et-e013.speaker: S04
et-e013.narration: For the first time, he doesn't have the next sentence ready.
et-e013.text: Millbrook toll. Southbound. I... may have driven towards Ridgeway. For the air. I didn't come into the city.

et-e011.speaker: S04
et-e011.text: The service call? A routine audit follow-up. The sensors should be tested every quarter. I simply made sure it was done.

et-e003.speaker: S04
et-e003.narration: He reads the line with the code on it twice.
et-e003.text: Four-seven. Anyone at head office could have had that code. It's written in a manual. Anyone.

et-e014.speaker: S04
et-e014.text: Bay rum? Half of Ridgeway wears bay rum, Detective. I really don't see what a cleaner's nose has to do with anything.

et-unmoved.speaker: S04
et-unmoved.text: I'm afraid that's outside my department. More tea?

dw-start.speaker: S05
dw-start.narration: Doreen Walsh has dusted the same leaf three times.
dw-start.text: I don't know nothing about any vault, love. I do the floors and the bins.

choices.label: Ask whether she worked over the holiday
Ask about the people who work here

dw-holiday.speaker: S05
dw-holiday.text: The branch was shut, wasn't it? I was at home with my Frank.

dw-staff.speaker: S05
dw-staff.text: Mr Pike's a gent. The chief clerk's all right. The auditor from head office tips nobody and smells like a barber's shop. Always has.

dw-e005.speaker: S05
dw-e005.narration: She sits down on the nearest chair.
dw-e005.text: Mr Pike asked me to do his office on Sunday. Cash. Don't tell head office, he'll get the sack. But listen: the corridor down to the vault was already mopped when I got there. Wet. And it smelled of bay rum. Nobody here wears bay rum.

dw-unmoved.speaker: S05
dw-unmoved.text: I wouldn't know about that, love. Is it important?
